headline: Van Veen holds off Aspinall from 7-2 up to win 16-14
standfirst: Gian van Veen reached the Grand Slam semi-finals, his best run here, after Nathan Aspinall pulled back from five legs down to 12-12.
body: Gian van Veen is into the semi-finals of the Grand Slam of Darts for the first time after beating Nathan Aspinall 16-14 in Wolverhampton on Saturday, a match in which he led 7-2 and then had to win it twice. His previous best at the event was a quarter-final in 2024.

Van Veen, ranked third in the world, started with four straight legs and moved ahead by five. Aspinall, 12th, closed the gap in the second half, helped by a 116 finish and a run of three legs that left the pair level at 12-12. From there it came down to who kept hold of his throw.
Van Veen did. He broke throw in leg 30 with a 16 finish to settle it, and the key moment came a leg earlier: a 32 checkout in 13 darts that put him 15-14 ahead and left Aspinall needing to break.

It was a match of very similar numbers. Van Veen averaged 95.17 and Aspinall 95.54, which means Aspinall lost with the higher average. Van Veen’s figure sits almost exactly on his 12-month average of 95.28; Aspinall, at 96.58 over the same period, was a little below his own. Aspinall hit 11 maximums to nine and his was the quickest leg, an 11-dart effort, but van Veen’s doubles were better at 44.4 per cent to 42.4.
The win guarantees van Veen £60,000, with Aspinall taking £35,000. Van Veen plays Michael van Gerwen in the semi-finals on Sunday at 2:45pm.
